newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: BURKE FOUND GUILTY - TO BE SENTENCED TODAY
Former Western Australian Premier, Brian Burke, will be sentenced later today, after being found guilty of seven counts of stealing ALP campaign funds.
In the Distirct Court in Perth, Judge George Sadleir found Burke had stolen 122-thousand dollars of ALP money to buy stamps for his personal collection.
The offences were committed while Burke was Premier in the 1980s.
Judge Sadleir accused Mr Burke of making false statements, concealments and fabrications in his unsuccessful defence of the charges.
Burke denied any wrongdoing.
In 1994, he was convicted of false pretences over parliamentary travel expenses and spent seven months in jail.
DEFENCE MINISTERS CALL FOR PNG TO SACK MERCENARIES
The Defence Ministers of Australia and New Zealand have called on Papua New Guinea to sack its mercenaries.
After talks in Canberra, Australia's Ian McLachlan and New Zealand's Paul East issued a communique describing the mercenaries as most unwelcome in the South Pacific.
Mr East told reporters that Australia and New Zealand would consider options for action if the Chan Government retained the mercenaries.
Mr McLachlan said Australia would look at all avenues to influence Papua New Guinea including financial and defence cooperation.
WELFARE SYSTEM WEED-OUT "NOT EASY": NEWMAN
The Department of Social Security says it's working independently to come up with a fair system to weed out social security cheats.
Minister Jocelyn Newman, says the new means test to be introduced for welfare payments, is not the same as that used for Austudy.
Hundreds of Austudy applications have been re-processed, because the means test used to determine eligibily didn't indicate their real financial position.
Senator Newman says coming up with a fair system isn't easy.
SYDNEY SHOPPING CENTRE ROCKED BY BOMB
The area surrounding a shopping centre in sydney's east has been declared safe, following the discovery of a bomb.
At around 11am, the Eastgate shopping mall at Bondi Junction was evacuated.
Police say the bomb didn't go off, but was discovered to be emitting hazardous gases.
12 people were taken to hospital, five others suffering breathing problems and eye irritations were treated at the scene.
The bomb has been removed and immmersed in water, to prevent an explosion.
MAN MAULED BY SHARK IN THE WHITSUNDAYS
In north Queensland, a 30-year-old man has been mauled by a shark in the Whitsundays.
Police say the man was swimming at Nara Inlet on Hook Island when he was attacked by what's believed to be a tiger shark.
He has wounds to his left arm.
The North Queensland rescue Helicopter Service is en route to Hayman Island to airlift the injured man to hospital.
It's the region's second shark attack this year.
A Victoria tourist was mauled by a shark while swimming at Whitehaven Beach last month.
YOUTH SUICIDE PREVENTION GROUP URGES DEPRESSION FIGHT
The chairperson of the Youth Suicide Prevention Advisory Group says young people should be taught how to overcome depression as early as primary school.
Dr Meg Smith has told a forum on youth suicide in Canberra, the best services for young people suffering from depression should be free, flexible and accessible such as telephone hotlines.
She says programmes successfully helping young people do exist, but often the information isn't shared well enough.
RACE CHIEF EXECUTIVE SAYS RACE WILL GO AHEAD
Melbourne Grand Prix Chief Executive, Judith Griggs, says most of the spill on the Albert Park race track has been cleared up.
Police are following several leads, including the possibility that a truck belonging to the Grand Prix Corporation leaked, causing oil to spread across the race track overnight.
However they suspect the leak was a sabotage attempt.
Ms Griggs says contingency plans went straight into operation, and has praised the work of those involved in cleaning up the leak.
TELSTRA NAMED AS SPONSOR OF SUPERLEAGUE

The battle between rival rugby league competitions has escalated with today's sposnorship announcement by Super League. The competition will be sponsored by Telstra who will go head to head with the Australian Rugby League's naming rights sponsor, Optus.
Super League Chief Executive John Ribot dismissed claims that the deal would create an even bigger rift between the two competitions.
He says the decision has nothing to do with the fact that they are rival telecommunications networks.
